questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=4 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=-3\end{aligned}\,\,[\begin{aligned}20 & a & 10 \\ c & 80 & -20 \\ 10 & -20 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}22 \\ b \\ 11\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of linear equations and its corresponding normal equation shown above. What is the value of $a-b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

The normal equation corresponding to $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -8 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -8 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}20 & -40 & 10 \\ -40 & 80 & -20 \\ 10 & -20 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}22 \\ -44 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
a-b+c=(-40)-(-44)+(-40)=-36.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -3 & -6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ above. If the normal equation corresponding to the system $Ax=b$ is given below, what is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 20 \\ 20 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The normal equation corresponding to $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -3 & -6 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}10 & 20 \\ 20 & 40\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=10+40+(-2)=48.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $15a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -4 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}40 & -20 \\ -20 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}10 & -5 & 1 \\ -10 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}10 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
15a+\frac{b}{c}=15\cdot \frac{1}{10}+\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{1}=2.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ -\frac{1}{5} \\ b\end{aligned}]\,+\,{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ c \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+2b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}Ax={A}^{T}b.
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -\frac{1}{5} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable.

From the second row, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{5}\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-\frac{1}{5}-{x}_{3}.
$$

From the first row, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -\frac{1}{5}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -\frac{1}{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+2b+c=1+2\cdot 0+(-1)=0.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a+2b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -8 & 2 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -8 & 2 & 0 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -8 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
2{x}_{1}-4(\frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3})+2{x}_{3}=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2+{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2+{x}_{3} \\ \frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+2b+c=1+2\cdot \frac{3}{2}+0=4.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}b \\ c \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,+\,{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $2a-3b-6c?$
questions.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b.
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}12 & -6 & 0 \\ -6 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}12 & -6 & 0 & 12 \\ -6 & 3 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=2{R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}12 & -6 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}12 & -6 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(1/6){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=(1/2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable.  

From the third row, we have

$$
{x}_{3}=1,
$$

and from the first row we obtain

$$
2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1+\frac{{x}_{2}}{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+\frac{{x}_{2}}{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
2a-3b-6c=2(\frac{1}{2})-3(1)-6(0)=-2.
$$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $3a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}54 & -18 \\ -18 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}54 & -18 & 12 \\ -18 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}54 & -18 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{9}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
3a+\frac{b}{c}=3\cdot \frac{2}{9}+\frac{(\frac{1}{3})}{1}=1.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $30a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}30 & -30 \\ -30 & 30\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}30 & -30 & 1 \\ -30 & 30 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}30 & -30 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{30}+{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{30}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{30} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
30a+\frac{b}{c}=30\cdot \frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{1}=2.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=6 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a-\frac{3b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -2 & -4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -2 & -4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & 18 \\ 18 & 36\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 18 & -9 \\ 18 & 36 & -18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 18 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-1-2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a-\frac{3b}{c}=-1-\frac{3(-2)}{1}=5.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=-3 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -5{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}30 & -60 \\ -60 & 120\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ -2 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
2a+\frac{b}{c}=2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{2}{1}=1.
$$

{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=3 \\ 2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=-2 \\ 3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $7a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}14 & -28 \\ -28 & 56\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -28 & -4 \\ -28 & 56 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}14 & -28 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{2}{7}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{7}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{7} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
7a+\frac{b}{c}=7\cdot (-\frac{2}{7})+\frac{2}{1}=0.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=4 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $4a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}14 & -14 \\ -14 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -14 & 7 \\ -14 & 14 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}14 & -14 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}+{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
4a+\frac{b}{c}=4\cdot (\frac{1}{2})+\frac{1}{1}=3.
$$
